description: A fungal leaf disease of maize that produces black tar-like spots on leaves. Severe infections reduce photosynthesis, grain filling, and can cause yield loss and stalk lodging.
symptoms: Small raised black spots on leaves that look like drops of tar
Black stromata on upper and lower leaf surfaces
Brown or tan lesions around black spots (fisheye lesions)
Large blighted areas when spots merge
Reduced grain filling and weak stalks in severe infections
favorable_conditions: Long periods of leaf wetness (at least 7 hours)
Presence of infected corn residues in the field
spread: Overwintering fungus on infected corn residues
Rapid spread between nearby fields under favorable weather
management: Monitor fields regularly for early symptoms
Harvest early if stalk strength declines
Use tolerant maize hybrids when available
Use crop risk prediction tools when available
biological_control: No widely adopted biological control currently available
chemical_control: Fungicide application between tasseling (VT) and silking (R1) stages
Fungicides such as prothioconazole or trifloxystrobin mixtures
Repeat application after 7–14 days if conditions remain favorable
prevention: Tillage to bury infected corn residues
impact: Yield losses up to about 50 bushels per acre reported in severe cases
Poor kernel filling and reduced ear weight
source: Tar Spot of Corn Research Publications
